items.title: music: extreme-fidelity synthesis of musical elements
items.abstract: Extreme-fidelity synthesis of musical elements, based on the MASS framework: psychophysical descriptions of musical elements in LPCM audio, expressed as equations and corresponding Python routines. State is updated at every sample, so a rendered sound is as close as it can be to the mathematical model that describes it.

items.title: Space - Time. Merging Physical or Iurian Coordinates and Spatial or Cartesian Coordinates to Unify and Harmonize Scientific Structure. Rev. 1
items.abstract: After decades of efforts to solve the fundamental structural question of science, this paper presents a critical analysis and proposes an alternative formulation. The predominant model of "space-time", central to modern physics, combines the three spatial coordinates with one temporal coordinate in a four-dimensional continuum (R³ + T¹). Although this model has great historical and theoretical importance, it has relevant limitations such as formal asymmetries, conceptual insufficiencies, and a visually unbalanced model, impeding clear, simple, and harmonious graphic representation of nature. These elements suggest weaknesses in the prevailing theories, which become evident when examined in the light of the structural unifications proposed in this study.             In this centennial scenario, the constitution of the Physical (or Iurian) Coordinates is proposed, conceived as a three-dimensional structure formed by Energy, Displacement (or Movement) and Time (EDT), whose components are intrinsically correlated, allowing a systematic combination/superposition between the Physical (or Iurian) Coordinates and the Spatial (or Cartesian) Coordinates. The unification harmonizes the two coordinates, configuring an innovative solution to the Gordian Structural Knot of the Edifice of Science . The current state of the art, the concepts of space-time reveal signs of structural instability, alerted by Thomas Kuhn’s studies, which emerge with greater intensity after this study. items.title: The Internet as Precedent: Architectural Lessons for Federated Computing
items.abstract: This technical note examines the Internet as an architectural precedent for Federated Computing. The analogy lies in preserving local autonomy by making only the conditions required across boundaries explicit. It is not a proposal for a Federated Computing protocol stack, nor a direct mapping from Internet protocols to governance functions.

items.title: MSKazemi/ExaMLOps: v0.50.0
items.abstract: Added The LXP node no longer builds what it deploys — CI does, once, and the node pulls it (opt-in behind EXAMLOPS_USE_REGISTRY ). lxp_release.sh ran docker compose up --build on every activation, which meant the deploy built from the internet on a node whose container egress has been firewalled before; that two deploys of one commit could differ; and — worst of the three — that rollback rebuilt . The path taken when the platform is already unwell could therefore produce an image that had never existed before. Images are now built once by build:images from a tree that passed every blocking check, pushed to the GitLab Container Registry, and pinned per release in .examlops-image.env , so reactivating an older release restores that release's own images rather than the current pipeline's. build_image.sh resolves each service's context and Dockerfile from the compose file itself, so the CI matrix names only services and cannot drift from what the deploy runs ( tests/unit/test_ci_image_matrix.py holds both directions). Unset, the pipeline and the node behave exactly as before. The same digests are mirrored outward for visibility — publish:ghcr and publish:dockerhub skopeo copy (never rebuild) to ghcr.io/mskazemi/* and docker.io/mskazemi/* , so a public image is bit-identical to the one production runs rather than a lookalike built at a different moment. Both allow_failure : a mirror outage must never redden a healthy deploy. items.title: Dilatant Dark Fluid: Toward a Unified Quantum-Hydrodynamic Origin of Lorentz Invariance, Gravity, and Cosmological Phenomenology
items.abstract: This work introduces the dilatant dark fluid (DDF), a pervasive cosmic cold dark medium comprising two coupled ultralight bosonic sectors: a superfluid \(\phi\) and a heavier dispersed phase \(\varphi\) undergoing stress-induced shear jamming, distinguishing the framework from earlier superfluid-vacuum models. The DDF's velocity-dependent dilatant response drives the local \(\varphi\) sector toward a saturated jammed state that supports the propagation at \(c\) of coupled transverse phonons identified with photons, while remaining asymptotically inaccessible to massive bodies. This constitutive response generates a jamming factor identical to the Lorentz factor, recovering Lorentz-form kinetic energy, clock rate, and length relations, alongside interferometric and resonator nulls. By governing both matter dynamics and operational measurement standards, the DDF provides a quantum-hydrodynamic material realization of geometric relativistic spacetime. The superfluid sector supports quantized vortices interpreted as particles; their circulation encodes spin and generates Bernoulli pressure gradients seeded near the core by the associated quantum potential, which upon many-vortex coarse-graining yield macroscopic gravitational acceleration. Painlevé-Gullstrand river coordinates geometrically encode this material dynamics in general-relativistic exterior solutions, recovering classical weak- and strong-field benchmarks, including leading Kerr-Lense-Thirring behavior. items.title: The Feasibility of Implementing Corporate Governance within the Framework of Sustainability in Agricultural Enterprises
items.abstract: Agricultural enterprises play a strategic role in ensuring food security, protecting natural resources, and sustaining rural livelihoods. However, the governance structures traditionally designed for large publicly listed corporations are often unsuitable for the diverse organizational characteristics of agricultural businesses. This study examines the feasibility of implementing corporate governance frameworks in agricultural enterprises from a sustainability perspective and proposes a governance model tailored to the sector's specific needs. Drawing on the theoretical foundations of agency theory, shareholder theory, and stewardship theory, the study evaluates governance challenges across three major organizational forms: family-owned farms, agricultural cooperatives, and agri-food companies. It argues that effective governance in agriculture must extend beyond financial performance to incorporate environmental stewardship, social responsibility, and long-term resilience. The analysis identifies key barriers to implementation, including limited governance awareness, resource constraints, regulatory gaps, and the heterogeneity of agricultural enterprises. Rather than advocating a uniform governance model, the study emphasizes the need for flexible and adaptive governance mechanisms that reflect differences in enterprise size, ownership structure, and institutional context. items.title: Gender Bias, Job Satisfaction, and Burnout Among Surgeons: Evidence from Korea
items.abstract: Purpose This study examines the relationships between formal and informal gender bias and burnout among surgeons, and it assesses whether job satisfaction mediates these associations differently for women and men. We conducted a nationwide survey of practicing surgeons in Korea, and the primary exposures were experiences of formal gender bias (e.g., hiring, pay, promotion, and leadership opportunities) and informal gender bias (e.g., exclusion from networks, limited access to resources, and derogatory or gendered comments). Key outcome variables were overall job satisfaction and burnout. Analyses were stratified by gender, and mediation models were used to explore indirect pathways through job satisfaction. Results Women surgeons reported substantially higher exposure to formal (62.5% vs. 11.3%) and informal (83.9% vs. 19.2%) gender bias than men. For both women and men, formal gender bias was associated with lower job satisfaction, and the relationship between formal gender bias and burnout appeared to operate indirectly through job satisfaction. Informal gender bias was also associated with lower job satisfaction for both genders. For men, informal gender bias retained a direct positive association with burnout after accounting for job satisfaction, while for women the association between informal gender bias and burnout was consistent with an indirect pathway through job satisfaction. Conclusions Gender bias is strongly linked to burnout among surgeons, operating largely through job satisfaction but with important gender-specific differences. Organizational strategies th

items.title: Protocol for a scoping review Artificial intelligence applied to bacterial biofilms: a scoping review of the evidence base and barriers to transfer to food processing environments
items.abstract: Registered protocol for a scoping review on artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning  (ML) applied to bacterial biofilms. The protocol specifies eligibility criteria, search strings for PubMed and Web of Science, a dual-reviewer screening procedure, and an extraction data framework. The review maps the full landscape of AI/ML for biofilm research across all settings (laboratory, clinical, in silico, industrial) to quantify what proportion has been conducted and/or validated in food processing environments.

items.title: Chinese-SkillSpan: A Benchmark for Competency Span Extraction from Chinese Job Advertisements
items.abstract: Online job advertisements can reveal changing skill demand only when competency mentions are recoverable as auditable text spans. Chinese lacks a large resource that combines explicit span-boundary rules with coverage of different recruitment genres. We present Chinese-SkillSpan, a corpus of 22,840 sentences from four Chinese recruitment sources. It uses a flat, ESCO-derived inventory of language skills and knowledge, knowledge, skills, and transversal skills and competences (LSKT), with Chinese-specific rules for minimal-complete, non-overlapping spans. Language models propose annotation drafts, but human reviewers retain authority over accepted offsets and types under a shared handbook. The benchmark uses identifier-strict scoring, exact and overlap-tolerant metrics, and source- and length-based analyses. Its evaluation reference is undergoing final human adjudication, so the current results are provisional estimates. The baseline study shows why the resource is challenging: exact extraction changes with Chinese boundary conventions, and accuracy varies across recruitment sources. Taken together, Chinese-SkillSpan contributes a multi-source span resource, a Chinese-specific annotation and evaluation protocol, and a reproducible baseline and diagnostic suite that exposes category, source, and boundary effects. Internal artifact names are confined to the supplementary reproducibility record. Project materials are maintained at https://github.com/AlfredJamesLi/chinese-skillspan-benchmark. The pretrained JobBERT-zh model is available at https://huggingface.co/AlfredJames/jobb

items.title: Ceremonial etiquette and official events
items.abstract: Ceremonial etiquette plays an important role in diplomatic protocol and international relations. It regulates the conduct of diplomats and officials during official events and state ceremonies. Proper observance of ceremonial etiquette helps maintain order, respect, and professionalism in interactions between representatives of different countries. Official events such as state visits, diplomatic receptions, international conferences, and signing ceremonies follow specific traditions and protocol rules. These rules include the order of precedence, formal greetings, respect for national symbols, and appropriate dress code. The purpose of this study is to analyze the significance of ceremonial etiquette and its role in the organization of official diplomatic events. The research also highlights how adherence to ceremonial protocol contributes to strengthening diplomatic relations and preventing misunderstandings in international communication.

items.title: A Study on Filipino Protocol Officers in Diplomatic Ceremonial Events
items.abstract: This study explored the roles and challenges encountered by Filipino Protocol Officers in managing diplomatic ceremonial events. These officers played a vital role in ensuring the seamless execution of formal state functions and diplomatic interactions, balancing respect for tradition with the evolving demands of modern diplomacy. Using qualitative methods, including semi-structured interviews and document analysis, the research examined the officers’ preparation strategies, adherence to established protocol, and navigation of cultural nuances. Key findings underscored the critical importance of meticulous planning, cultural sensitivity, and effective inter-agency coordination. The study also identified major challenges, such as communication gaps, conflicting customs, and workload-related stress, along with the strategies employed to address them. Overall, this study contributed to a deeper understanding of the complexities involved in diplomatic protocol and offered recommendations for improving ceremonial event management practices in the Philippines.

items.title: THE ROLE OF PROTOCOL IN INTERNATIONAL RELATIONS AND PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION
items.abstract: The article examines the functions and role of state and diplomatic protocol and analyzes its theoretical foundations and practical application in international relations and public administration.The evolution of protocol from the court ceremonial of European monarchies to modern democratic state protocol based on the principle of sovereign equality of states is explored.It is demonstrated that protocol should be understood not merely as a set of etiquette rules but as a complex political and legal system that regulates official interaction, ensures predictability of diplomatic communication, and symbolically represents state authority in both international and domestic contexts.Three fundamental functions of modern protocol are identified and analyzed: regulatory, symbolic, and communicative.The regulatory function lies in establishing clear procedures and algorithms for organizing official meetings, negotiations, ceremonies, and other forms of diplomatic interaction, which helps prevent conflicts and misunderstandings among participants.The symbolic function manifests itself in the visual representation of state sovereignty, dignity, and legitimacy through the use of national symbols as well as ceremonial practices such as official visits and inaugurations.The communicative function is interpreted as a specific form of non-verbal political communication through which states transmit signals of respect, support, partnership, or, conversely, dissatisfaction and distancing in the international arena.Particular attention is paid to the transformation of modern protocol towar

items.title: Ayala Ω Framework H6-D: Preregistered Angular-Acceptance × Initial-Final Interference Stress Test of the Frozen 756–781 MeV Region
items.abstract: The protocol prespecifies a 25 MeV target window (0.756–0.781 GeV) and equal-width adjacent lower and upper control windows, together with the primary acceptance-weighted Ω-window contrast and angular/IFI diagnostic. It also freezes the primary KLOE-II-like small-angle radiative-return configuration, statistical and uncertainty reporting plan, benchmark requirement, anti-tuning rules, reproducibility requirements, and outcome-classification framework. H6-A remains frozen and is not redefined by this analysis. Alternative windows, cuts, observables, generator settings, or other modifications introduced after inspection of the H6-D results will be treated as exploratory. This protocol was frozen on September 2, 2026, before evaluation of the exact H6-D target-window statistics. It does not claim resolution of the muon g−2/HVP discrepancy, discovery of new physics, or proof of a causal mechanism.

items.title: The identifiable resolution of cellular counterfactual prediction — Source data
items.abstract: This record archives the numerical source data accompanying the manuscript “The identifiable resolution of cellular counterfactual prediction.” The study investigates context geometry compression (CGC), the dissociation between accurate cellular-state prediction and recovery of context-specific intervention effects. Its analyses distinguish measurement, information and prediction resolution. Key findings include limited context-specific recovery despite near-complete experimental coverage, greater recovery from pathway-level readouts of the same predictions, and saturation of functional personalization performance within a compact baseline-transcriptomic representation. The archive contains 20 figure source-data tables corresponding to Main Figures 1–6, Extended Data Figures 1–9 and Supplementary Figures 1–5, together with Supplementary Tables 1–6 in CSV and XLSX formats. It includes numerical estimates, uncertainty summaries, panel identifiers, source references, table captions, dataset accessions and resource-version information. Undefined quantities are retained as such, and metric definitions and statistical interpretations are documented in the accompanying files. These derived results originate from analyses of publicly available primary human CD4+ T-cell Perturb-seq data, official State cytokine and drug-response prediction artifacts, Tahoe-100M, paired lymphoblastoid cell-line data with independent ARCHS4 reprocessing, and colorectal-cancer organoid pharmacogenomic data. Upstream datasets, annotation resources and model artifacts

items.title: Verified Factual Reference Base and instrument registry of the Cognitive Warfare Information Analysis Laboratory No. 1
items.abstract: Verified Factual Reference Base and instrument registry, CWIAL No. 1, version 0.1.0 A reference base of propositions whose factual status has been verified against the documented record, with the sources supporting each verification and a registry of the survey instruments used to measure belief in them. It serves as the reference standard in belief displacement measurement: a displacement is only meaningful against a stated true value, and this file set holds those values, their evidential basis and their verification dates. Propositions are graded TRUE, FALSE or CONTESTED. This is not a catalogue of false claims. Contents. Three tables and their codebook. vfrb_propositions.csv holds the register, one row per proposition, with its truth value, evidential tier, verification dates and the basis for its assignment. vfrb_sources.csv holds the sources supporting each truth value, with a reliability grade and access date. instruments.csv holds the survey instruments used to obtain belief readings, with fieldwork date, documented bias and the base actually used. vfrb_codebook.csv defines every field of all three tables, with type, whether it is required, permitted values, and the five source reliability grade definitions. README, CHANGELOG, CITATION.cff and LICENSE complete the set. Inclusion criteria. items.title: The identifiable resolution of cellular counterfactual prediction — Analysis code
items.abstract: This record archives the analysis code accompanying the manuscript “The identifiable resolution of cellular counterfactual prediction.” The study identifies context geometry compression (CGC): models can preserve cellular identity and shared perturbation responses while failing to recover context-by-intervention interactions. It distinguishes measurement resolution, information resolution and prediction resolution, and examines the resolution at which cellular counterfactual responses are empirically recoverable. In the tested settings, high post-perturbation state accuracy and near-complete experimental coverage did not guarantee context-specific response recovery. The same predictions recovered more signal in pathway coordinates than in the full gene-expression vector, while compact baseline-transcriptomic representations retained most of the functional drug-ranking performance in patient-derived colorectal-cancer organoids. The archive contains 26 frozen scientific implementation bundles, configurations, split metadata, statistical resampling and null procedures, input requirements and execution documentation. These cover primary human T-cell prediction, official State prediction-artifact evaluation, Tahoe experimental completion and operator analyses, paired lymphoblastoid response prediction, pathway-resolution analyses, mechanism-aligned multimodal analyses and colorectal-cancer organoid personalization. items.title: Partial Order Semantics and Operational Semantics for Strand Spaces, via Rocq
items.abstract: Rocq mechanization accompanying "Partial Order Semantics and Operational Semantics for Strand Spaces, via Rocq" by Matteo Busi, Riccardo Focardi, Joshua Guttman, and Flaminia Luccio, submitted to JLAMP. This release extends the StrandsRocq framework with: an inductive characterization of bundles, with soundness and completeness theorems; a CPSA-style protocol syntax embedded in Rocq; a structured operational semantics for protocol execution; correspondence theorems showing that reachable thread pools and bundles carry exactly the same information; a computational labeled semantics, including the realization of compatible enumerations. Build with dune build . Requires dune>=3.21 and Rocq 9.1.0.

items.title: FAIR-D / CARE-D documented governance dataset for Indigenous-language digital resources in Mexico
items.abstract: Research dataset accompanying the study “Beyond openness: FAIR, CARE, and documented Indigenous data governance in digital language infrastructures in Mexico.” The dataset operationalizes the public documentary visibility of FAIR and CARE-related practices in digital resources associated with Indigenous languages spoken in Mexico. It includes the 12-resource main analytical sample, an extended matrix containing excluded and sensitivity cases, the FAIR-D/CARE-D coding instrument, a source audit, and a reproducibility script for the principal descriptive statistics. Scores represent publicly documented evidence as of 20 August 2026 and must not be interpreted as direct measures of substantive ethical compliance or as evidence that undocumented practices were absent.

items.title: Loss of Environmental Awareness in Businesses: Organizational Blindness
items.abstract: Organizations operating in increasingly dynamic and uncertain environments face growing challenges in recognizing and responding to external changes. This study examines the phenomenon of organizational blindness, defined as the systematic inability of organizations to perceive, interpret, and act upon critical environmental signals despite the availability of relevant information. Drawing on theories of organizational cognition, managerial attention, sensemaking, and strategic management, the study explores the cognitive, structural, and cultural mechanisms that contribute to this deficiency. It analyzes key concepts including bounded rationality, dominant logic, cognitive rigidity, organizational inertia, information-processing failures, organizational silence, and institutional isomorphism, demonstrating how these factors collectively restrict strategic adaptation. To illustrate the practical consequences of organizational blindness, the study examines the well-known cases of Kodak, Nokia, and Blockbuster, showing how established routines, overconfidence, and rigid mental models prevented these organizations from responding effectively to technological and market transformations. The findings suggest that organizational blindness results not from a lack of information but from failures in attention, interpretation, communication, and decision-making processes. items.title: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum FN029 ameliorates atopic dermatitis in dysbiotic mice through activation of retinol and glutathione metabolic pathways in gut-associated lymphoid tissues
items.abstract: This dataset contains numerical source data and figure-building values for the manuscript “Lactiplantibacillus plantarum FN029   ameliorates atopic dermatitis in dysbiotic mice through activation of retinol and glutathione metabolic pathways in gut-associated lymphoid tissues”.  The deposit includes data for Main Figures 1-11 and Supplementary Figures S1, S2, and S4. Each figure archive contains the corresponding figure directory, a README.md file, and numerical or tabular data describing the panels, variables, units or numerical scales, sample organization, and interpretation notes. FILENAME_MAPPING.tsv records the normalized public filenames and their former staged paths. The dataset includes individual-animal measurements, values underlying plotted means and error bars, image-derived quantitative measurements, RNA-seq, proteomics, metabolomics, microbiome, qPCR, immune-marker, histological, and network-analysis data. Raw 16S rRNA sequencing reads associated with Figures 8-9 are available from the NCBI Sequence Read Archive under BioProject accession PRJNA1463385.
